items.stem: Clinical decision support is best described as a tool that:

options.text: Provides timely information to support, not replace, clinician decisions
options.rationale: Correct: CDS augments clinician judgement with relevant information.

options.text: Automatically issues treatment without clinician involvement
options.rationale: CDS supports clinicians; it does not act autonomously in patient care.

options.text: Replaces the electronic health record entirely
options.rationale: CDS works with, not instead of, the record.

items.explanation: Correct: CDS augments clinician judgement with relevant information.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO risks are commonly associated with poorly designed clinical decision support? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Alert fatigue from too many low-value alerts
options.rationale: Correct: excessive alerts lead clinicians to ignore them.

options.text: Automation bias where users over-trust the suggestion
options.rationale: Correct: over-reliance on automated advice is a recognised risk.

options.text: Guaranteed elimination of all diagnostic error
options.rationale: CDS does not eliminate error; it is itself a source of risk if misused.
Confirmation remains necessary regardless of CDS quality.

options.text: Removing the need to monitor outcomes
options.rationale: Ongoing safety monitoring is still required.

items.explanation: Correct: excessive alerts lead clinicians to ignore them.

items.stem: The 'five rights' of clinical decision support emphasise delivering the right information to the right person in the right format through the right channel at the right:

options.rationale: Correct: timing within the workflow is the fifth 'right'.
Font size is not one of the five rights.
Billing is unrelated to the five rights of CDS.
Server location is not part of the five rights.
